summary: A heavy Pfister euro where you sail a ship around a Caribbean course, choosing at each stop whether to fight, deliver goods, build influence, or advance along multiple card-driven tracks. The story-driven event deck and layered systems make each of the four rounds feel eventful, at the cost of a fairly steep rules and iconography load.
praised: gorgeous production and strong table presence
satisfying variety of viable strategies across combat, trading, and influence
narrative event/quest layer adds unusual flavor for a euro
criticised: heavy rulebook and iconography overwhelm many new players
significant card-draw luck affecting available bonuses
long individual turns can create downtime for others
can feel like several games stapled together

interaction.kind: shared track position, competitive influence and combat
interaction.detail: Ship position on the shared course determines turn order and who gets first pick at locations, and players directly compete for influence and city control, but each player's hand, resources, and personal board development remain private. Conflict at sea is possible but the bulk of play is parallel engine-building.

scoring.how_you_win: After 4 rounds, players total VP from city-influence majorities across three nations, movement-track bonuses, permanent cards, delivered goods, story progress, and leftover coins; the highest total wins.
